title: Shadowbox Coach: Foundation to Fight Camp
tagline: 70 days, two phases, one camera. Earn your way from fundamentals to fight-ready — every round measured, every promotion proven.
gate_text: You are promoted to Fight Camp when your Phase 1 week-5 telemetry clears all five gates. These are the app's own tracked stats — check them on your stats screen after every session. (1) arm_punch_pct at or under 25%, averaged over your last 10 tracked rounds of week 5: Fight Camp opens with hip-and-shoulder rotation drills and dumbbell punch work that assume your power already comes from the torso — arm-punching a third of your shots under camp load just hardens the fault. (2) guard_height_sw at or above 0.85 shoulder-widths as a session average on every tracked day of week 5, no single-day exemption: Fight Camp includes light sparring, and a guard that only stays up when the corner coach nags is a safety liability against a partner. (3) avg_retraction_ms at or under 350 ms, averaged over your last 10 tracked rounds of week 5: the camp demands 4-to-8-punch chains off the pendulum step, and a chain is only as long as your slowest hand's trip back to guard. (4) punches_per_round at or above 120 per 3-minute round (40 per minute), taken as the median across the five shadowbox rounds of your final week-5 shadowbox day: camp partner work runs 6 rounds of 4 minutes, and if you cannot hold that pace for 3 minutes you will finish 4-minute rounds with degraded technique. (5) avg_power at or above 55 as a session average on that same final shadowbox day, with round 5 fading no more than 10 points below round 1: the floor proves your mechanics produce real force, the fade cap proves it is conditioned rather than front-loaded — clean-but-slow is not fight-ready. All five gates read week-5 data only; strong early weeks do not bank credit, and a missed gate means repeating week 5 until the numbers hold.
coach_guidance: The corner coach cues from exactly one theme at a time — the active week's focus — so trust the narrowness: in week 1 it will only talk stance and movement even if your guard drops, because guard is week 2's job. Press START DAY before every session so the coach loads the right theme and the round clock matches the day's prescription; the timer drives the main tracked block (bag rounds, sparring rounds, shadowbox rounds), while shorter sub-drills listed in a day's blocks are self-timed off the written prescription. After each session, read your stats against the current week's theme, not against everything at once: weeks 1 and 4 (stance, shifts and angles), watch punches_per_round and avg_power trend as your feet organize your offense; week 2 (defense and body work), guard_height_sw is the number that matters — it should rise and then stop moving; week 3 (pivots and combinations), watch avg_retraction_ms fall as chains get longer; week 5 (integration and control), all five gate stats at once, because this is the only week the gates read. Only camera-visible punching rounds are scored — lifts, calisthenics, tire work, and heavy-bag-only strength blocks are untracked by design, so a quiet stats day after a lift day is correct, not broken. In Phase 2, keep the same habit but change the question: not "is my form right" but "do my numbers hold in the last round" — compare round 1 to the final round on every long-round day, and treat a widening gap as a conditioning signal, not a technique one. Rest days are tracked as rest: do not shadowbox on them to farm stats; gate windows exclude them anyway.
signoff_notes: Signed off to ship, with the following recorded for the next revision. Source fidelity is strong: the verifier confirmed all 154 source_drill citations verbatim against lessons.v1.json, repaired 32 concatenated citations to single canonical lines, and confirmed no invented or silently dropped drills; canonical OCR typos and genuine source duplications (Workout #11 twice, Workout #15 reused, #12/#16 nonexistent) are preserved by design and should be annotated as source artifacts in the UI rather than "fixed". Open issues, by priority: (1) App safety bug — rest and lift days ship rounds=0/roundSec=0 and the timer code does not guard against START DAY on them; the app must no-op or show a rest screen instead of entering a zero-length loop. (2) Beginner load — Phase 1 week 1 day 1 puts a raw beginner on six 3-minute bag rounds with slip/roll defense before any punch is taught (jab/cross first appears w1d4), day 3 demands 7x3 bag rounds, and no day teaches punch mechanics explicitly; a future revision needs an on-ramp or explicit prerequisite note, since 6 days/week with no deload is intermediate load sold as Foundation. (3) Timer expressiveness — the single day-level rounds/roundSec/restSec only fits one block per day; sub-schemes (2-minute technique rounds with 30s rest, 6x1min/20s tennis-ball work, 45/15 intervals) live in prose and contradict the day header, forcing athletes off the in-app timer on exactly the days that matter. Per-block timing is the top feature request. (4) Vague blocks — "Strength block A/B", "Lift block A/B", "Supplemental rounds", and "Timed round" name no exercises and are unrunnable without guessing. (5) QA content defects to patch: basic w1d1 and w3d1 carry a 3-vs-6-round contradiction between bag sub-drills and the day timer; basic w3d1 has a truncated round-3 prescription ("3 slips plus") and a missing hanging-leg-raise rep count; competitive w1d1 leaks transcription/provenance notes into three user-facing prescriptions; competitive w2d6 encodes the endurance circuit as 3x60s/30s while w4d6 encodes the identical prescription as 30x60s/30s (w4d6's 30 rounds also flagged as a likely parse error needing semantic review). (6) Gate machinery gap — Phase 2 day entries repeatedly reference "gate windows" and "five phase gates" (w1d6, w2d6, w3d6, w4d6, w4d7, w5d6, w5d7), but the shipped app's only gate counts completed Phase 1 days and is not telemetry-based; either implement telemetry gating as specified in the architect's design or strip the framing from Phase 2 copy. w5d6/w5d7 also mislabel the competitive camp "Phase 1", contradicting the on-screen PHASE 2 header. (7) Minor progression copy errors in Phase 2: w4d4 and w4d5 call previously-seen drills "new" (pendulum rounds since w2d4, 9x1 freestyle since w3d5) and w4d5 claims sparring "stretches to" 6x4 though it has held that scheme since w2d5. Source curriculum owner for all content questions: Jai (boxing.dharmicdata.org).

gates.threshold: <= 25% averaged over the last 10 tracked rounds of Phase 1 week 5
gates.why: Phase 2 opens with 'FIGHTING STNCE: HIP AND SHOULDER ROTATION FOCUSED DRILL' and dumbbell punch work that presumes power already comes from the torso. An athlete still arm-punching a third of their shots will reinforce the fault under the camp's added load, so rotation mechanics must be fixed before entry.

gates.threshold: >= 0.85 shoulder-widths session-average on every tracked day of Phase 1 week 5 (no single-day exemption)
gates.why: Phase 2 weeks 2-4 include 'LIGHT SPARRING WITH SINGLE PUNCHES' and 'FREESTYLE LIGHT SPARRING'. A guard that only stays up when the corner coach nags is a safety liability against a partner; week 2's Defense and body work theme must be automatic, not prompted, by the end of week 5.

gates.threshold: <= 350 ms averaged over the last 10 tracked rounds of Phase 1 week 5
gates.why: The camp's Specialized preparation weeks demand '4-8 PUNCHES OFF THE PENDULUM STEP' — combination chains only work if each hand is back in guard fast enough to fire the next shot. Slow retraction caps chain length and leaves the athlete open between punches.

gates.threshold: >= 120 per 180-second round (40 punches/min), median across the five 3-minute shadowbox rounds of the final Phase 1 week-5 shadowbox day
gates.why: Phase 2 stretches partner work to 'PARTNER WORK (6 ROUNDS OF 4 MINUTES)'. An athlete who cannot hold 40 punches/min through 3-minute rounds after 35 days lacks the work capacity for 4-minute rounds and will complete the camp's volume with degraded technique.

gates.threshold: >= 55 session-average with round 5 no more than 10 points below round 1 on the final week-5 shadowbox day
gates.why: Peak performance week scores fight-simulation rounds where power must survive fatigue. The floor of 55 confirms hand speed plus torso rotation are producing real force; the round-1-to-round-5 fade cap confirms it is conditioned, not front-loaded. Complements the arm_punch_pct gate: low arm-punch % with low power means slow correct mechanics, not fight-ready mechanics.

phase1.title: Foundation 35 (KO Basic Program)
phase1.intro: Phase 1 — Foundation 35. Five weeks, one theme per week: stance and movement, defense and body work, pivots and combinations, shifts and angles, then integration and control. The rhythm never changes: two technique days, one high-volume bag day (seven 3-minute rounds, one minute rest — the classic amateur clock), one virtual-sparring day against a new opponent archetype each week (the slugger, the puncher, the southpaw, the tall guy, the short guy), one lift day, and one full rest day. Every drill comes straight from the KO Boxing basic program — nothing invented, nothing softened. Here is what makes this phase different from a video course: the camera is watching. Every shadowbox and sparring round is scored — punch counts, punches per minute, guard height, how fast your hands snap back, how much of your power comes from your torso versus your arm. Phase 1 is not about surviving the volume. It is about making the fundamentals show up in the numbers when nobody is cueing you: a guard that lives at your chin, punches that start at the hips, hands that return fast enough to throw the next shot. You do not graduate on day 35. You graduate when the stats say so — see the gates below.

phase2.title: Fight Camp 35 (KO Competitive Camp)
phase2.intro: Phase 2 — Fight Camp 35. This is the KO competitive camp, periodized the way a real camp is. Week 1 is general preparation: the engine gets rebuilt around rotation — hip-and-shoulder drills, dumbbell punch work, everything reinforcing power from the ground up. Weeks 2 through 4 are the hard middle, specialized preparation: rounds stretch past the amateur standard to 6 rounds of 4 minutes of partner work, light sparring enters, and you drill 4-to-8-punch chains off the pendulum step with feints layered in. Week 5 is peak performance: volume tapers and everything converts to fight simulation — three 3-minute rounds against an opponent you picture in front of you and fight. Each week closes with endurance work (or active recovery in week 5) and a rest day. The app changes its job here too. It stops nagging you about guard height and arm-punching — that was Phase 1's business, and you already proved it. Now the telemetry pushes output: punch density under longer clocks, power that holds up in round six, retraction speed inside long combination chains. There is no exit gate at the end. Day 35 is the end — you arrive fight-ready or you repeat the week that broke you.
